title: Kenyan Wedding Biryani
community: Coastal Kenyan communities — Muslim weddings and celebrations
author: Chef Amina Hassan

relatedDish.note: Wedding Biryani is the grandest, most laboriously prepared version of KEN004 (Kenyan Biryani). The dum cooking method, the saffron-infused layer, and the fried onion garnish elevate the basic biryani technique to its highest expression for the most important celebration.

desc: Kenyan Wedding Biryani — the grandest expression of coastal Kenyan biryani. Fragrant basmati rice layered with spiced beef or chicken, saffron, fried onions, and caramelised cashews, slow-cooked dum-style under a sealed lid. The celebration dish of coastal Kenyan Muslim weddings.
longDesc: Wedding biryani on the Kenyan coast is one of the most elaborate culinary preparations in the country — requiring a full day of cooking, multiple skilled cooks, and ingredients of the highest quality. The dum cooking method (sealing the pot with dough and slow-cooking with coals on the lid) creates a self-contained oven that infuses every grain of rice with the fragrance of the spiced meat below.
ingredients: 1.5 kg beef or chicken — marinated overnight in yogurt and spices
3 large onions — thinly sliced and deep-fried until golden
½ cup cashews — fried until golden
½ tsp saffron — soaked in 4 tbsp warm milk
equipment: Dough for sealing (flour and water) or foil
steps: Marinate meat in yogurt and all marinade spices overnight.
Parboil rice with whole spices until 70% cooked — the grains should still have a bite. Drain.
Cook the marinated meat in ghee until almost cooked through — 30—35 minutes for beef.
Layer in the pot: meat at the bottom, half the rice over the meat, fried onions, cashews, raisins, remaining rice, saffron milk drizzled over top, remaining ghee.
Seal the pot lid with dough or heavy foil.
Cook over very low heat for 25—30 minutes (dum cooking).
Remove seal. Fold gently to mix the layers slightly — preserve some colour variation.
chefTips: Parboiling the rice to 70% is the most critical step — undercooked and it will be hard in the final dish; overcooked and it will be mushy.
The dum seal is what makes biryani — it traps all the fragrance inside the pot.
Saffron is expensive but non-negotiable for wedding biryani — it provides the characteristic golden colour and floral aroma.
commonMistakes: Fully cooking the rice before dum — it overcooks during dum and becomes mushy.
Incomplete sealing — steam and fragrance escape.
cookingScience: The dum cooking technique creates a sealed environment where the trapped steam cooks the partially-cooked rice while simultaneously absorbing the aromatic compounds from the meat and spices below. The pressure inside the sealed pot slightly elevates the boiling point of water, cooking the rice more efficiently.
sustainabilityTips: Saffron is the world's most expensive spice by weight — use precisely what is needed, no more.
reheating: Reheat covered with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Saffron contains crocin — a potent antioxidant.
culturalNote: Wedding biryani on the Kenyan coast is a cultural institution — the dish that marks the most important celebrations of coastal Muslim communities. The skill required and the quality of the result are a direct expression of the family's pride and love for their guests.
